To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the development and spread antimicrobial resistance can be reduced or prevented by limiting the use of antimicrobials in animals.

(1) antimicrobial resistance is a major problem in the human and in the veterinary habitat; (2) the application of antimicrobial substances is the main risk factor in the development and the spread of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria; (3) the use of antimicrobials in veterinary medicine has to be controlled in order to minimize the development of antimicrobial resistancies; (4) risk management measures in veterinary medicine should be applied to reduce the development and the dissemination of antimicrobial-resistant microorganisms
there are many risk management measures that are already in place to reduce the development and spread antimicrobial resistances.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of risk management strategies in the field of antimicrobial resistance in the food chain.
the identification and evaluation of strategies and risk management measures for the prevention and control of antimicrobial resistance in bacteria in the food chain.
the development of risk management strategies for the prevention and control of antimicrobial resistance in the food chain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of antimicrobials is a necessary and unavoidable part of animal husbandry.

the use of antimicrobials in animals is a risk factor for the development and dissemination of resistance in the food chain, but that there is no evidence that the use of veterinary antimicrobials poses a direct threat to human health.
the use of antimicrobials in food-producing animals should be limited and restricted.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of antimicrobials should be limited, and that the use of the most important antimicrobials in human medicine should be restricted to a minimum in food-producing animals, especially in those animals with direct contact to humans.
the use of antimicrobials in animals is not the only source of antimicrobial resistance in the food chain.

a reduction of the use of the most critical antimicrobial agents in veterinary medicine will be the main risk management strategy to prevent the development and spread and of antimicrobial resistance in the human and the veterinary habitat.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reduction of antimicrobial use is a necessary, yet not sufficient condition for controlling antimicrobial resistance.
there is an urgent need for the development and evaluation of risk management strategies for the control of antimicrobial resistanc.
there are many risk management tools and options available to control the spread of antimicrobial resistant pathogens.
